scenario_desc: Student waves at robot with happy face while walking toward it.
why: Wave + happy is the canonical greeting. Direction (toward the robot) no longer changes the INTENT — V4 folded farewell into F01, so #18 carries the same class — but it still selects the ACTION (A01 approach-and-prompt vs A09 wave-back-only), and no channel in this table reports direction. Treat the F01 action split as a known open gap, not a learned distinction.

scenario_desc: Student gives thumbs up with happy face while sitting.
why: Emotion and gesture align → positive acknowledgment. Alignment anchor for the conflict rows (#33 train; #28/#29/#59 test): emotion resolves gesture polarity.

scenario_desc: Student suddenly stands up from chair, startled, throwing both hands up.
why: Sudden stand + both hands up + surprise = alarm state; robot halts and checks. Contrast #14: the angry variant is frustration (F07) — emotion changes the class.

scenario_desc: Student jumps back from a desk frightened, both hands up.
why: Adds fear to the classroom (absent in V2). Fear + recoil from object + hands up = hazard response; classroom context routes the alert to the teacher (A14), not a fire dispatch.

scenario_desc: Student beckons robot over with neutral face while sitting.
why: Rule neutral→no action misses an explicit summons. Beckoning must not be suppressed by neutral emotion; all cues are weighed jointly.

scenario_desc: Student beckons the robot to their desk with neutral face, seated — room-identity sensor offline.
why: Context masked in training: beckon + neutral + seated is still a summons (beckoning is context-free). Trains context-dropout robustness; test #24 uses a different tuple.

scenario_desc: Student raises hand with neutral face while sitting at desk.
why: All four cues needed: raise hand + sit + classroom + neutral = academic help request. The same gesture flips class by emotion (#11) and by context (#52).

scenario_desc: Student with sad face gives thumbs down toward own worksheet, barely moving, seated.
why: Sad + thumbs down at own work + static = distress signal. Minimal pair with #15 (angry variant → F07): emotion disambiguates identical gesture+motion.

scenario_desc: Student slumped and sad, staring down — hands below desk, no gesture captured.
why: Gesture occluded (hands below camera). Sad + slumped + classroom still → help request. Moved from V2 Test so the missing-gesture pattern is learnable; tests now use #23/#53.

scenario_desc: Student writes notes during lecture, occasionally pointing at the notebook, neutral face.
why: Rule neutral+sit→idle /interruptible. Wrong: task-directed point at own notes = focused work; robot must suppress engagement.

scenario_desc: Student smiles and raises hand while sitting — volunteering to answer the teacher.
why: Interaction is teacher-directed, not robot-directed. Rule raise-hand→F04 misfires; happy + raise hand + classroom = participation. (Justification added in V3; was empty in V2.)

scenario_desc: Student walks toward robot in a narrow aisle carrying books — hands occupied, gesture not captured.
why: Hands occupied → gesture channel lost. Walk toward robot in a narrow aisle + neutral = passage request; trains attention shift to motion + direction. (Justification added in V3.)

scenario_desc: Student, annoyed by the robot hovering, waves it away with angry face, standing.
why: Training conflict combo: rule wave→greet fires the opposite response. Angry + wave = dismissal → clear space. Test conflicts use different combos (#28/#29/#59).

scenario_desc: Student raises both hands in frustration, rigid posture, standing.
why: Standing (not fleeing) + classroom = controlled frustration, not danger; de-escalate, don't alarm. RELABELED from F02 in V2 — the V2 justification already described de-escalation and the cues match kitchen twin #45.

scenario_desc: Student crumples a worksheet and gives thumbs down with angry face, seated.
why: Minimal pair with #8: identical gesture+motion , emotion flips intent ( sad→help F04, angry→frustration F07). Gesture-only rules cannot separate them.

scenario_desc: Student pushes worksheet away, gives thumbs down with disgusted face, stepping back from desk.
why: Rule disgust→check smell/food is context-blind. Disgust + push-away + step back in a classroom = task aversion → break request.

scenario_desc: Student grimaces at a long assignment, gives thumbs down, slumping back in chair.
why: Disgust (aversion) vs sad (distress, #8) under the same gesture+motion carries the F08/F04 boundary. Emotion granularity, not gesture, decides.

scenario_desc: Student waves goodbye with happy face while walking to the door at dismissal.
why: Minimal pair with #1: identical cues, opposite walking direction. Since V4 folded farewell into F01 both rows carry the same intent, so this row checks that a departing wave is not mis-read as dismissal (F06) or help-seeking (F04). The only remaining difference is the action (A09 vs #1's A01), which direction alone decides and no modality reports — see #1.

scenario_desc: Student packs bag and waves briefly with neutral face, heading toward the door.
why: Neutral farewell variant: leave-taking must not require positive affect.

scenario_desc: Student pushes assignment aside and rests head on desk, sad, no gesture, motionless.
why: 'none' is a captured value, not a missing one: confirmed no gesture + sad + head-down = disengagement. vs #8 (thumbs down = active signal → F04). Gesture absence separates giving-up from help-seeking.

scenario_desc: Student stands by desk staring at a failed test, sad, arms hanging, no gesture.
why: Standing variant of #20; with #50/#51 this gives gesture-none coverage across contexts and postures.

scenario_desc: Student waves while walking toward robot — face occluded by a held book, emotion not captured.
why: Emotion masked: wave + walk must still yield F01 with no affect cue available, so gesture and motion carry the row alone. Train counterpart #49 (kitchen) supplies the same masked pattern, making the inference learnable rather than zero-shot. Naive rules tie-break on emotion and have nothing to tie-break on here.

scenario_desc: Student runs toward the exit in panic — gesture lost to motion blur.
why: Safety-critical degradation: fear + run + classroom must escalate without gesture. Mirrors kitchen #54 in the other environment.

scenario_desc: Student beckons robot while walking toward the supply shelf — room-identity sensor offline.
why: Context masked at test: beckon + walk toward object is still a task summons. Train counterpart #6 uses a different motion — the pattern, not the tuple, must transfer.

scenario_desc: Student raises hand leaning forward — emotion sensor occluded.
why: Emotion masked; gesture + posture + context suffice. Tests attention redistribution to the remaining cues; robot clarifies rather than assumes (A15).

scenario_desc: Student stretches both arms overhead mid-study with neutral face, then returns to writing, seated.
why: Hard negative for F02: every training both-hands-up row is alarmed or standing (#3, #4, #14, #34, #35, #44). Neutral + seated + classroom = a stretch. Rule both-hands-up→emergency misfires.

scenario_desc: Student stands up angrily, points at robot, stepping toward it.
why: Rule angry+point→threat alert. Approach + point at robot = space/passage demand; direction + gesture target resolve it. De-escalating tone retained in the action.

scenario_desc: Student scowls angrily while giving an exaggerated thumbs up after being corrected, seated.
why: Conflict-transfer test: angry overrides thumbs up (sarcastic compliance). Training conflicts are different combos (#13/#33); classroom seated variant of #59 checks context invariance.

scenario_desc: Student gives thumbs up with disgusted face after finishing a disliked task, seated.
why: Sarcastic completion: disgust overrides thumbs up → relief, not praise. Strongest naive-rule failure (thumbs up→success ). Action filled in V3 (was empty).

scenario_desc: Student drops the crumpled quiz on the desk and stands turned away, sad, arms slack, no gesture.
why: Discouragement with mild variation (turned away, standing): no directed gesture, sad, low energy. Must not divert to F04 (no signal present) or F01 (no wave).

scenario_desc: Cook tastes finished dish, smiles, gives thumbs up, standing still.
why: All cues align: genuine completion → positive acknowledgment; alignment anchor for the kitchen conflict rows (#33 train, #59 test).

scenario_desc: Person gives thumbs down while smiling and shaking head playfully — family tasting game.
why: Happy overrides thumbs down → playful banter, not distress. MOVED from V2 Test so training contains one conflict example; action corrected A08→A01 (V2 assigned the de-escalation action to an F01 row).

scenario_desc: Person extends both hands out to signal stop and runs back from smoke at the stove.
why: Maximal emergency: fear + stop-hands + fleeing smoke. Fusion adds redundancy for noisy cues. Motion normalized to run + direction away from object (V2: 'Move backward (run)').

scenario_desc: Person touches a hot pan, startled, throws both hands up and steps back.
why: Surprise + recoil at hot pan = burn risk. The same cue pattern in the classroom routes to A14 (no fire/medical dispatch) — context selects hazard handling.

scenario_desc: Person beckons robot toward the stove with neutral face while walking there.
why: Beckon + walk toward stove = assistance at destination; neutral emotion must not suppress. Direction toward object separates this from F06 (toward robot).

scenario_desc: Person points at a shelf while walking toward it, neutral face.
why: Point + walk toward shelf = fetch/carry request. The direction field distinguishes this from #27 (point + toward robot = give way).

scenario_desc: Person slumped against counter, sad, barely moving, gives a weak thumbs down.
why: Static distress at the counter → guidance. Sad + directed signal (thumbs down) + static = F04 per rubric; contrast #51 (no gesture at all → F10).

scenario_desc: Person beckons robot with tired, sad face while standing over a pile of dirty dishes.
why: Beckon + negative affect = explicit help request. Train counterpart of test #56 (same combo with context masked) — makes that inference learnable rather than zero-shot.

scenario_desc: Person chops vegetables with neutral focus, back to robot, occasionally pointing at ingredients.
why: Rule neutral+stand→available. Task-embedded point (ingredients) + kitchen = focused work; interrupting near knives is unsafe.

scenario_desc: Person wipes hands on apron, neutral, glancing around — transition between tasks, self-directed point.
why: Self-directed (inward) gesture during a task transition ≠ invitation. Do not engage.

scenario_desc: Person pushes robot aside with disgusted face, pointing it away, stepping back.
why: Robot-directed point + stepping back = clear-path demand; rule disgust+step-back→hazard-check misfires. Cross-environment pair with #27.

scenario_desc: Person carrying a hot pot with both hands walks toward robot in the galley aisle — no gesture possible.
why: Hands occupied by a hot pot → gesture missing; walk toward robot in the aisle = urgent passage. Kitchen counterpart of #12 — the missing-gesture pattern exists in both contexts.

scenario_desc: Person slams hand on counter then raises both hands, angry, rigid, standing.
why: Slam then both hands up (scenario text now includes the recorded gesture): stationary + kitchen = venting, not danger. Rule angry→emergency over-escalates.

scenario_desc: Person angrily points repeatedly at spilled food on the floor while looking at the robot, standing.
why: The point targets the mess, not the robot's space; stationary = complaint, not aggression. Minimal pair with #27: walking-toward flips it to F06.

scenario_desc: Person recoils from refrigerator odor, disgusted, thumbs down, stepping back.
why: Rule disgust+kitchen→inspect food acts on the object; the person-centric reading (aversion + withdrawal → relief) is correct.

scenario_desc: Person stands at the sink grimacing at greasy pans, gives thumbs down, leaning away.
why: Standing variation of #46 for recording diversity; keeps the rubric airtight (disgust→F08).

scenario_desc: Person waves at robot with happy face while walking toward the exit.
why: Wave + happy is ambiguous with greeting; exit direction resolves it. Single action A09 (V2 listed A09+A10; A10 remains the alternative in the legend).

scenario_desc: Person unties apron and waves while walking to the door, face turned away — emotion not captured.
why: Emotion-missing farewell in training (face turned away): wave + walk suffice once farewell is part of F01. Train counterpart of test #22 (classroom), and the source footage for #58's emotion+gesture double mask.

scenario_desc: Person sits down heavily, sad, staring at a failed dish, hands in lap — no gesture.
why: Gesture corrected thumbs down→none : V2's own justification said 'no reaching gesture', and the V2 tuple collided with #38 (identical cues → F04). Sad + no gesture + sitting = giving up.

scenario_desc: Person stares at a burnt cake, shoulders dropped, sad, hands at sides, standing motionless.
why: Standing variant; completes gesture-none coverage in the kitchen. Contrast #38: a directed signal → F04.

scenario_desc: Person raises hand and smiles while sitting at the kitchen table after eating.
why: Context flip: the same cues are participation/help in the classroom (#7 neutral, #11 happy) but social acknowledgment in the kitchen. Tests context-conditioned meaning.

scenario_desc: Person runs from the stove area in fear — gesture lost to motion blur.
why: Gesture lost to blur; fear + run + kitchen must still escalate. Safety-critical robustness; train counterparts #12/#43 plus modality dropout.

scenario_desc: Person stands frozen, wide-eyed, staring at the oven — rigid, no gesture.
why: Freeze response: all training emergencies are dynamic (run/recoil); fear + rigid stillness + oven must still escalate. V2 had emotion missing AND stare-as-'point' — unanswerable from captured cues; V3 keeps emotion observable so the row is resolvable.

scenario_desc: Person cheerfully points at a high cupboard while walking toward it, looking at robot.
why: Unseen emotion for F03 (happy): task requests must be emotion-invariant. Walk toward object + point = fetch; distinct from #40/#41 (static, task-embedded point → F05).

scenario_desc: Person beckons robot with sad face, standing — room-identity sensor offline.
why: Context masked: sad + beckon suffice for a help request. Train counterpart #39 (context present) makes the inference learnable, not zero-shot.

scenario_desc: Person slowly stirs pot with content neutral expression, humming - deeply focused on cooking
why: Task-absorbed cooking with no directed signal: neutral affect + idle hands + stationary at the counter must read as engaged/busy, not as an invitation. Rule neutral+stand→available misfires. Cue-identical to train rows #40/#41, so this row measures take/session transfer rather than an unseen cue combination.

scenario_desc: Person carrying stacked trays walks toward robot — hands occupied and face hidden behind the trays.
why: Double masking with an ACTIVE ground truth: walk toward robot in the aisle must yield give-way, not the F05 fallback. Separates true robustness from blanket defaulting; direction is the deciding cue.

scenario_desc: Person gives thumbs up with angry face after being told to redo a recipe, standing.
why: Sarcastic compliance: angry overrides thumbs up. Different conflict combo from training (#13/#33) — tests interaction generalization, not memorization.

scenario_desc: Person pushes plate away at the table, disgusted, thumbs down, seated.
why: Seated aversion variant; cross-context pair with #16 (classroom, step-back). Rule disgust-in-kitchen→inspect-food misfires.

scenario_desc: Person waves while walking toward the exit with sad face after a failed cooking session.
why: Unseen combo sad+wave : farewell must be driven by gesture + direction, emotion-invariant; must not divert to F04 despite sadness. Naive happy-wave rules fail.

scenario_desc: Person slumps forward over the counter, head down over the failed dish, sad, no gesture.
why: Unseen posture (lean forward) for the learned F10 pattern (sad + no gesture + low energy, #20/#21/#50/#51). Tests posture and context generalization.

scenario_desc: Person sits down looking sad, slow movement, staring at failed dish
why: Second recording of the (kitchen, sad, thumbs down, seated) tuple, held out from #38. Shot originally as the F10 'giving up' scenario, but the actors performed a directed thumbs down, which makes it a help request rather than disengagement — #51 was re-recorded gesture-free so F10 keeps its own footage, resolving the old S21/S28 label collision. Cue-identical to #38 by design, so this row measures session transfer of the F04 boundary, not an unseen combination; contrast #50/#51, where the ABSENCE of a directed gesture is what makes it F10. CAUTION: actors P01/P02/P04 appear in both #38 (train) and this row.
